title_en: The Meaning of Unelaborated Negation and Detailed Affirmation
body_ar:
ما معنى النفي المجمل والإثبات المفصل الذي يرد دائما في كتب أهل السنة؟

أن النفي المجمل هو أن ينفي الله تعالى عن نفسه بعض الأمور على سبيل الإجمال ولا يفصل فيها، مثل قوله تعالى: {لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ (3) وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ (4)} [الإخلاص] فهذا نفي إجمالي ومثل قوله: {لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ} [الشورى 11] فهذا نفي إجمالي لكن لم يرد تفصيله، فلم يرد مثلا في آية ولا في حديث: ليس بجوهر ولا بجسم ولا عرض كاللون والطعم إلى غير ذلك من النفي المفصل، كذلك الإثبات جاء مفصلا، فالله سبحانه وتعالى يقول في كتابه: {اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ (255)} [البقرة]

ويقول تعالى: {وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ (14) ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ (15) فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ (16)} [البروج] وغير هذا من التفصيل مثل ما جاء في حديث أبي هريرة أن النبي (ص) قال: (إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما مائة إلا واحدا من أحصاها دخل الجنة)، وجاء في بعض طرقه زيادة هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر الخالق البارئ المصور الغفار القهار الوهاب الرزاق، الفتاح العليم القابض الباسط الخافض الرافع المعز المذل السميع البصير الحكم العدل اللطيف الخبير الحليم العظيم الغفور الشكور العلي الكبير الحفيظ المقيت وفي رواية المغيث الحسيب الجليل الكريم الرقيب وفي رواية القريب، المجيب الواسع الحكيم الودود المجيد الباعث الشهيد الحق الوكيل القوي المتين وفي رواية المبين الولي الحميد المحصي المبدئ المعيد المحيي المميت الحي القيوم الماجد الواجد الواحد الأحد الصمد القادر المقتدر المقدم المؤخر الأول الآخر الظاهر الباطن الوالي المتعالي البر التواب المنتقم العفو الرؤوف مالك الملك ذو الجلال والإكرام المقسط الجامع الغني المغني المانع الضار النافع النور الهادي البديع الباقي الوارث الرشيد الصبور. فكل هذه أسماء مقتضية لصفات وجاء ذلك على سبيل التفصيل لا على سبيل الإجمال، فهذا إثبات مفصل ونفي مجمل.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

مصير من لم تبلغه دعوة نبي

من تربى في بلاد الكفر ولم يسمع قط بالإسلام ولم تبلغه الدعوة فمات على ذلك فما قول الشرع فيه؟

أن الله تعالى يقول: {وما كنا معذبين حتى نبعث رسولا} فمن لم تبلغه هذه الدعوة يبعث يوم القيامة فيبعث إليه النبي (ص) يمتحن به، فإن صدقه دخل الجنة وإن كذبه دخل النار.
body_en:
What is the meaning of unelaborated negation and detailed affirmation, which comes up constantly in the books of the people of the sunnah?

Unelaborated negation is that God, exalted, negates certain things of Himself in an unelaborated way and does not go into detail in them — as in His words, exalted: {He did not beget, nor was He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him} (Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ 112:3–4). This is an unelaborated negation. And as in His words: {There is nothing like Him} (Sūrat al-Shūrā 42:11). This is an unelaborated negation, but its detail has not come down: there has not come down, for instance, in any verse or in any hadith: He is not a substance, nor a body, nor an accident such as colour or taste, and so on with the rest of detailed negation.

Likewise the affirmation came in detail. For God, glorified and exalted, says in His Book: {God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting. Neither drowsiness takes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. Who is there that can intercede with Him except by His leave? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except as He wills. His seat extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation does not weary Him; and He is the Most High, the Magnificent} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:255).

And He says, exalted: {And He is the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Throne, the Glorious, Doer of whatever He wills} (Sūrat al-Burūj 85:14–16). And there is other detail besides this, such as what came in the hadith of Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'God has ninety-nine names — a hundred less one. Whoever enumerates them enters the Garden.' And in some of its lines of transmission there came an addition: He is God, other than whom there is no god; the Most Merciful (al-Raḥmān), the Compassionate (al-Raḥīm), the King (al-Malik), the Holy (al-Quddūs), the Source of Peace (al-Salām), the Granter of Security (al-Muʾmin), the Watchful (al-Muhaymin), the Mighty (al-ʿAzīz), the Compeller (al-Jabbār), the Supremely Great (al-Mutakabbir), the Creator (al-Khāliq), the Originator (al-Bāriʾ), the Fashioner (al-Muṣawwir), the Ever-Forgiving (al-Ghaffār), the Subduer (al-Qahhār), the Bestower (al-Wahhāb), the Provider (al-Razzāq), the Opener (al-Fattāḥ), the All-Knowing (al-ʿAlīm), the Withholder (al-Qābiḍ), the Expander (al-Bāsiṭ), the Abaser (al-Khāfiḍ), the Exalter (al-Rāfiʿ), the Giver of Honour (al-Muʿizz), the Giver of Abasement (al-Mudhill), the All-Hearing (al-Samīʿ), the All-Seeing (al-Baṣīr), the Judge (al-Ḥakam), the Just (al-ʿAdl), the Subtle (al-Laṭīf), the All-Aware (al-Khabīr), the Forbearing (al-Ḥalīm), the Magnificent (al-ʿAẓīm), the Forgiving (al-Ghafūr), the Appreciative (al-Shakūr), the Most High (al-ʿAlī), the Great (al-Kabīr), the Preserver (al-Ḥafīẓ), the Sustainer (al-Muqīt) — and in one transmission, the Helper (al-Mughīth) — the Reckoner (al-Ḥasīb), the Majestic (al-Jalīl), the Generous (al-Karīm), the Watcher (al-Raqīb) — and in one transmission, the Near (al-Qarīb) — the Responsive (al-Mujīb), the All-Encompassing (al-Wāsiʿ), the Wise (al-Ḥakīm), the Loving (al-Wadūd), the Glorious (al-Majīd), the Raiser of the Dead (al-Bāʿith), the Witness (al-Shahīd), the Truth (al-Ḥaqq), the Trustee (al-Wakīl), the Strong (al-Qawī), the Firm (al-Matīn) — and in one transmission, the Manifest (al-Mubīn) — the Protector (al-Walī), the Praiseworthy (al-Ḥamīd), the Enumerator (al-Muḥṣī), the Initiator (al-Mubdiʾ), the Restorer (al-Muʿīd), the Giver of Life (al-Muḥyī), the Giver of Death (al-Mumīt), the Living (al-Ḥayy), the Self-Subsisting (al-Qayyūm), the Noble (al-Mājid), the Finder (al-Wājid), the One (al-Wāḥid), the Unique (al-Aḥad), the Eternal Refuge (al-Ṣamad), the Able (al-Qādir), the Omnipotent (al-Muqtadir), the Advancer (al-Muqaddim), the Delayer (al-Muʾakhkhir), the First (al-Awwal), the Last (al-Ākhir), the Manifest (al-Ẓāhir), the Hidden (al-Bāṭin), the Governor (al-Wālī), the Exalted (al-Mutaʿālī), the Source of All Goodness (al-Barr), the Ever-Relenting (al-Tawwāb), the Avenger (al-Muntaqim), the Pardoner (al-ʿAfū), the Kind (al-Raʾūf), the Owner of All Sovereignty (Mālik al-Mulk), the Possessor of Majesty and Honour (Dhū al-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām), the Equitable (al-Muqsiṭ), the Gatherer (al-Jāmiʿ), the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghanī), the Enricher (al-Mughnī), the Preventer (al-Māniʿ), the Bringer of Harm (al-Ḍārr), the Bringer of Benefit (al-Nāfiʿ), the Light (al-Nūr), the Guide (al-Hādī), the Incomparable Originator (al-Badīʿ), the Everlasting (al-Bāqī), the Inheritor (al-Wārith), the Guide to the Right Way (al-Rashīd), the Patient (al-Ṣabūr).

All of these are names entailing attributes, and that came by way of detail and not by way of the unelaborated. So this is detailed affirmation and unelaborated negation.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

The fate of one whom no prophet's call has reached

One who was brought up in the lands of unbelief and never heard of Islam at all, and whom the call did not reach, and who died upon that — what does the revealed law say about him?

God, exalted, says: {And We were not to punish until We had sent a messenger} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:15). So whoever this call did not reach is raised on the Day of Resurrection, and a prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is sent to him and he is tested by him: if he believes him, he enters the Garden; and if he denies him, he enters the Fire.

flags.context: the pair the whole first fatwa is about
flags.note: STYLE GUIDE §8 APPLIES THROUGHOUT THIS RECORD. This is a creedal text about God's attributes, not a legal text, and no five-rulings vocabulary may be read into it. The glossary fixes mujmal as 'unelaborated' and mubayyan as 'clarified' in their usul senses; mujmal is used here in the parallel kalām sense and the glossary rendering has been kept for consistency. 'General' in option 3 would collide with ʿāmm, which is a different technical term.

flags.arabic: ليس بجوهر ولا بجسم ولا عرض كاللون والطعم
flags.context: the Sheikh's example of the detailed negation that scripture does NOT contain
options: He is not a substance, nor a body, nor an accident such as colour or taste
He is not an essence, a physical body, or a quality
leave the kalām terms in transliteration
flags.note: IMPORTANT — THIS IS A CLAUSE ABOUT WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY. jawhar, jism and ʿaraḍ are the technical vocabulary of kalām — substance, body and accident. The Sheikh's point is precisely that this detailed philosophical negation is NOT found in the Qur'an or the hadith, and that scripture negates only in an unelaborated way. An English reader could easily take the clause for a creedal assertion by the Sheikh rather than for his example of what revelation withholds, so the negative framing of the sentence must be unmistakable. He is not ruling the detailed negation out of court either; he says only that it has not come down. Nothing has been added in either direction.

flags.context: how the Sheikh introduces the list of the ninety-nine names
options: preserve his framing exactly: an addition found in some lines of transmission
present the list as part of the prophetic report
flags.note: CRITICAL — THE SHEIKH'S OWN QUALIFICATION MUST NOT BE LOST. He does not present the enumerated list as the words of the Prophet. He says it came as an ADDITION in some of the lines of transmission (ṭuruq) of the report, which is the standard and careful way of marking a passage that hadith scholars widely regard as a narrator's interpolation rather than prophetic speech. Dropping or flattening that framing would turn a qualified citation into an unqualified one and would misrepresent him on a point he was careful about. The three internal variants he notes ('and in one transmission …') have likewise been kept.

options: render each name into English with the transliteration in brackets, as done here
flags.note: HOUSE STYLE APPLIED, BUT EVERY ITEM NEEDS REVIEW. The style guide is explicit that an untranslated Arabic term standing alone is not a translation, so each name has been given in English with the Arabic in brackets. But single-word English renderings of the divine names are interpretive to a degree that no other part of this corpus is: several of them (al-Muhaymin, al-Ṣamad, al-Wājid, al-Mājid, al-Barr, al-Muqīt) have no settled English equivalent and have been rendered on the most common understanding. None of the ninety-nine is in the glossary. This list should be fixed centrally, once, by a qualified reviewer, and the fixed forms applied across the whole corpus; the renderings here should be treated as a first draft, not as settled.

flags.context: two unrelated fatwas served under one title
options: flag as compound and let the site present the two separately
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The page carries a second and entirely unrelated fatwa, on the fate of one whom no prophet's call has reached, under its own heading. It is invisible from the record's title, and it is a substantial creedal position in its own right — the Sheikh holds that such a person is tested on the Day of Resurrection rather than being consigned either way, which is a reported position among the theologians and not the only one. Not split unilaterally; the site should present the two as distinct items so that the second is findable.

flags.arabic: فيبعث إليه النبي (ص) يمتحن به، فإن صدقه دخل الجنة وإن كذبه دخل النار
options: a prophet is sent to him and he is tested by him
the Prophet is sent to him and he is tested by him
flags.note: AMBIGUOUS REFERENT. al-nabī with the abbreviation (ص) after it would normally mean Muhammad specifically, but the doctrine the Sheikh is stating — the testing of those whom no call reached — is usually framed in terms of a messenger sent to them at the gathering, not necessarily Muhammad. The Arabic will bear either reading and the Sheikh says nothing further. The English has taken the indefinite reading, which is the less committing of the two, and the ambiguity is flagged rather than resolved.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-27 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The Qur'anic quotations carry their sūrah names in square brackets and verse numbers in the source; the references have been rendered per house style. The quotation in the second fatwa is given without a reference and the reference has been supplied; the wording matches Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:15.

'His seat' renders kursiyyuhu in Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:255. This is itself a disputed attribute verse and no interpretation has been supplied, which is consistent with the Sheikh's own argument in this record that scripture affirms in detail without going beyond what it says.
The Sheikh attributes the report of the ninety-nine names to Abu Hurayra and names no collection and gives no grading; nothing has been supplied.
'The people of the sunnah' renders ahl al-sunnah in the questioner's phrase.
